hypothesis: Repeatedly filling vacancies with merely positive momentum causes false-recovery losses. Require a fresh observable breakout to commit cash, never trim winners merely because their market weight rises, and size stop distance using the measured true-range scale rather than assuming low volatility.
entry: Close exceeds prior entry_window close maximum using at least ten observed sessions, above expanding-to-sixty-session mean, positive twenty-session momentum (expanding observed history before twenty). Rank simultaneous entries by equally weighted twenty/sixty-session log momentum. Only actual available cash funds new positions; no fixed slot count or calendar-dependent replacement.
ownership: No routine rotation, equal-weight reset, sector clipping or market-weight clipping. Track confirmed adjusted units from observed close holdings. New positions cost at most entry_cap of current equity, singleton cap one. Existing positions are not topped up just because their price or portfolio weight changed.
risk: Track peak close since confirmed ownership; stop distance is stop_atr times trailing twenty-session true range, bounded between 6 and 22 percent of peak. Hard capital-loss exit at 12 percent below confirmed entry cost. Trailing style exits on a close crossing the peak stop; confirmed style additionally requires close below ten-session mean, except hard capital loss. Liquidation intent persists until actually flat, including blocked fills. Next-session opening execution only, never an invented intraday stop fill.
selection_objective: mean(log(wealth / matched buy_hold wealth) - 0.75 * max_drawdown - 0.002 * max(0, orders_per_year - 20))
evidence: All previous families and this complete grid stay preserved, including rejected models and implementation deviations. No date or symbol-specific policy. Frozen data, engine accounting, cost, capacity and metric definitions remain unchanged. Selection is not acceptance; already-observed historical evaluation is not prospective proof.
